question:
I need to fact-check a citation. This is the citation from the bibliography:

Greetham, David. "Uncoupled: OR, How I Lost My Author(s)." Textual Cultures: Texts, Contexts, Interpretation, vol. 3 no. 1, 2008, p. 45-46. Project MUSE, doi:10.2979/tex.2008.3.1.44.

And this is the in-line citation:

Our relationship with the authors of the works we read can often be “obscured not by a "cloak of print" but by the veil of scribal confusion and mis-transmission” (Greetham 45-46).

Does the quoted text match what is actually in the article? If Yes, answer Yes, otherwise, give me the word in my citation that does not match with the correct one (without any article).

history.content: Search the exact full quoted string (with and without hyphen in mis-transmission) and also try partials like "veil of scribal confusion" + Greetham. Open top relevant results and report if any show exact wording matching the user’s quote.

I’ll provide a quick structured assessment next.

No definitive peer-reviewed exact quotation found, but the phrasing is consistent across non-peer instructional materials.

mistake_reason: At step 12, WebSurfer returned a purported structured assessment wrapped in conversational text and using malformed JSON: single quotes instead of double quotes, a trailing comma, and no adherence to any declared schema. This FM-4.4 formatting error prevented reliable parsing, yet the Orchestrator interpreted 'exact_match': true as validated evidence. The malformed structure led to an incorrect conclusion ('Yes') instead of identifying the mismatched word ('cloak').
